Use the /marimo-pair skill to pair-program on a running marimo notebook.

Connect to the notebook at: http://localhost:2718/

Use `execute-code.sh --url http://localhost:2718/` from the marimo-pair skill to execute code in the notebook.

content.text:
---
name: marimo-pair
description: >-
  Drive a live marimo notebook as a workspace: run Python in the same kernel
  the user does, inspect live notebook state, and commit durable notebook
  changes. Use when the user wants to start a marimo notebook or pair on an
  active marimo session.
allowed-tools: Bash(bash **/scripts/discover-servers.sh *), Bash(bash **/scripts/execute-code.sh *), Read
---

marimo is a reactive Python runtime for building reproducible Python programs
(marimo notebooks). Cells are connected by the variables they define and
reference. Running a cell re-executes dependents in dataflow order. The active
runtime holds the kernel namespace, cell state, and dataflow graph. The
notebook (`.py` file) is the artifact the kernel writes from that state while a
session is running.

A user interacts with the same runtime via a notebook UI with cells, outputs,
and widgets.

**WARNING. The active runtime is the source of truth.** During a session, you
SHOULD NOT modify the associated `.py` file directly. File edits WILL NOT reach
the active kernel or user, and the kernel may overwrite them on save. Use
`marimo._code_mode` (`cm`) for notebook changes. Reading disk is fine, but
prefer `ctx.cells[...].code` for current cell code.

## Connect to a Notebook

Use the bundled script (`bash scripts/execute-code.sh`) or MCP
(`execute_code(...)`) to run Python in a live marimo kernel.

If the user provides a notebook URL, target it directly:

```bash
bash scripts/execute-code.sh --url http://localhost:2718 -c "print('connected')"
```

Use `-c` only for short one-liners. For multiline code or code containing
quotes, backticks, `$`, or braces, use a single-quoted heredoc:

```bash
bash scripts/execute-code.sh --url http://localhost:2718 <<'PY'
import marimo._code_mode as cm

async with cm.get_context() as ctx:
    cid = ctx.create_cell("x = df.head()")
    ctx.run_cell(cid)
PY
```

When code already lives in a file, pass the file path:

```bash
bash scripts/execute-code.sh --url http://localhost:2718 /tmp/code.py
```

If no target is provided, find or start a session. First look for a running
session with `bash scripts/discover-servers.sh`, MCP `list_sessions()`, or
local process context. When multiple sessions are possible, target with
`--url`, `--port`, or `--session`.

If no server is running and the user wants a notebook, start marimo with
`--no-token` (and without `--headless`) so it auto-registers for discovery. The
notebook UI must be open before there is an active session for `execute-code`
to target. The right way to invoke marimo depends on context (project tooling,
global install, sandbox mode). If the notebook file contains a PEP 723 `#
/// script` header, it MUST be opened with `--sandbox` — otherwise marimo
ignores the inline dependencies. See
[finding-marimo.md](reference/finding-marimo.md) for the full decision tree and
[execution-context.md](reference/execution-context.md) for scripts, MCP, and
shell quoting.

## Scratchpad Scope

`execute-code` evaluates Python in marimo's scratchpad: a temporary namespace
with a shallow copy of the kernel globals. Notebook variables are available by
name, but new top-level bindings and rebindings are discarded after each call.
In-place mutations to notebook-owned objects can persist because those names
still reference live objects.

Each call reports stdout and stderr from the scratchpad, plus console output
from notebook cells it causes to run, including reactive descendants.

### Ordinary Python

Use ordinary Python in the scratchpad to inspect variables, sample data, test
transformations, probe APIs, check imports, and read widget state.

```python
print(df.head())

x = 10
print(x)
```

Here `df` comes from notebook globals, while `x` is a scratchpad-local binding.
`x` exists for this call only and WILL NOT be added to notebook globals.

### Persist with `cm`

Top-level scratchpad assignments and rebindings are temporary. To persist work,
including new variables, you MUST submit changes through `marimo._code_mode`
(`cm`).

`marimo._code_mode` is a PRIVATE, UNSTABLE agent API (note the leading
underscore). It exists for tools like this skill to drive a live kernel from
the scratchpad. DO NOT import it from notebook cells, library code, or
anything a user would run — methods can change or disappear across marimo
versions and kernels. Treat every `import marimo._code_mode as cm` as
scratchpad-only.

At session start, inspect what `cm` exposes in the active kernel:

```python
import marimo._code_mode as cm

help(cm)
```

Open a code-mode context to queue notebook changes.

```python
import marimo._code_mode as cm

async with cm.get_context() as ctx:
    cid = ctx.create_cell("x = df.head()")
    ctx.run_cell(cid)
```

The scratchpad supports top-level async code. Use `async with` directly;
wrapping it in `asyncio.run(...)` is unnecessary and can conflict with the
kernel's event loop.

After this block exits and the new cell runs, `x` is notebook state. Later
scratchpad calls can read `x` by name. Code later in the same scratchpad call
should read `ctx.globals["x"]`, because the scratchpad namespace was copied
before the cell ran.

Inside the context, queued mutation methods are synchronous. Call them
directly; do not `await` them. Each call queues an operation for marimo to
apply when the context exits normally. If the block raises, the queue is
discarded.

On clean exit, marimo applies packages, validates and applies structural cell
changes, runs queued cells, then may run dependents. Validation is only
structural since queued cell runs can still error. `create_cell` and
`edit_cell` change notebook structure only. Use `run_cell` to execute. 

`create_cell` currently defaults to `hide_code=True`, which collapses the code
editor in the UI. Pass `hide_code=False` if the user wants created cells to
be visible without manually expanding them.


## Marimo Rules

marimo imposes a small contract on notebook code so it can keep the notebook as
a directed acyclic graph (DAG):

- **No cycles** - cells cannot depend on each other in a cycle.
- **No public redefinitions across cells** - each name has one owning cell.
- **No wildcard imports** - `import *` prevents static analysis of definitions.

These rules keep the kernel, UI, and saved artifact consistent.

When `cm` submits a cell body, marimo parses its top-level definitions and
references. A top-level name enters the graph unless it is private with a
leading underscore.

```python
# Public definitions: values, total, i, value, mean
values = np.array([1, 2, 3])
total = 0
for i, value in enumerate(values):
    total += value
mean = total / len(values)
mean
```

```python
# Public definition: mean
_values = np.array([1, 2, 3])
_total = 0
for _i, _value in enumerate(_values):
    _total += _value
mean = _total / len(_values)
mean
```

Use private names for intermediates that no other cell should read. Public
names define the notebook-level dataflow. If a `cm` edit violates the contract,
marimo rejects the structural change and returns the validation error.

## The Notebook's Shape

A notebook is an ordered collection of cells. `ctx.cells` is the document view
and `ctx.graph` is the dataflow view.

```python
for cell in ctx.cells:
    cell  # .id, .code, .name, .config, .status, .errors

ctx.cells["setup"]         # by name
ctx.cells[0]               # by position
list(ctx.cells.keys())     # all IDs, in notebook order
```

Cell IDs are opaque strings which can be queried from the notebook or captured
from `cm` return values:

```python
cid = ctx.create_cell("df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')")
print(cid)   # e.g. 'Hbol'
```

Alternatively, cells can be assigned and referenced by `name`. The graph can be
used to understand its role in the dataflow.

```python
for cid, impl in ctx.graph.cells.items():
    impl  # .defs, .refs   (sets of public names)

ctx.graph.descendants(cid)   # cells that re-run when this one changes
ctx.graph.ancestors(cid)     # cells this one depends on
```

In marimo, deletes are *destructive* so it can be useful to query the
descendants prior to deleting to understand it's impact.

## Writing Notebook Changes

The graph contract keeps marimo able to run and save the notebook. Passing
those checks alone does not guarantee a useful artifact. Committed cells should
still be readable, rerunnable, and editable.

Make durable edits that reuse the notebook's existing names, imports,
dependencies, and UI model. Don't be lazy. Avoid one-off workarounds that pass
`cm` validation but leave a brittle notebook.

### Cell Bodies

Submit the code that belongs in the cell.

- **Submit cell contents** - `create_cell` and `edit_cell` take cell contents,
  not saved-file `@app.cell` wrappers.
- **Read before replacing** - for now, another editor may change a cell between
  scratchpad calls. Before `edit_cell`, read the current body from
  `ctx.cells[...]` and submit the full replacement.
- **Reuse notebook imports** - if `np` already exists, use it or edit the owning
  import cell. DO NOT add `import numpy as _np` just to bypass the graph.
- **Define public names intentionally** - use public names for values later
  cells should reference. Use private `_name` bindings or function locals for
  same-cell intermediates.
- **Define each public name once** - a public name has one owning cell.
  Reassigning it in another cell fails with `Multiply-defined names`; edit the
  owning cell or give the result a new name. See
  [gotchas.md](reference/gotchas.md).
- **Run cells deliberately** - `create_cell` and `edit_cell` change structure
  only. Queue `ctx.run_cell(...)` when the cell should execute.

### Prefer `cm`-Managed Changes

Use `cm` APIs when they exist. Avoid direct file edits, shell package commands,
and scratchpad-only state for changes that should persist.

- **Do not edit the `.py` artifact** - DO NOT use `Edit`, `Write`, or
  `NotebookEdit` on the notebook file during a live session. Use
  `ctx.edit_cell(...)` even for small changes.
- **Manage packages through `cm`** - use `ctx.packages.add()` or
  `ctx.packages.remove()` instead of direct `uv` or `pip`; confirm
  non-obvious dependency changes.
- **Avoid transient paths** - persisted cells should not depend on `/tmp/...`
  unless the work is intentionally transient.
- **Delete deliberately** - deleting a cell removes globals it defines. Reuse
  empty cells when convenient and delete cells left empty after edits.

### UI and Widgets

Inspect the object before changing it. Different UI objects update through
different paths.

- **Set `mo.ui.*` through `cm`** - use `ctx.set_ui_value(element, value)` inside
  `cm.get_context()`.
- **Set anywidget traitlets directly** - synced traitlets are Python
  attributes, for example `widget.value = 5`.

For designing custom visual or interactive output, see
[rich-representations.md](reference/rich-representations.md).

## References

- [execution-context.md](reference/execution-context.md) — scripts, MCP, auth, startup, and shell quoting
- [finding-marimo.md](reference/finding-marimo.md) — choosing the right marimo invocation
- [gotchas.md](reference/gotchas.md) — name redefinition, cached module proxies, and notebook traps
- [rich-representations.md](reference/rich-representations.md) — custom widgets and visualizations
- [notebook-improvements.md](reference/notebook-improvements.md) — improving existing notebooks

[README.md#3B50]
1:# Multilingual BPE tokenizer — India Wikipedia
2:
3:This repository is the solution to the tokenizer assignment below (English, Hindi, Telugu, Sanskrit; shared 10 000-token vocab; score $1000 / (X_{\max}-X_{\min})$).
4:
5:---
6:
7:## Assignment
8:
9:Your assignment would be to pick India's page on Wikipedia in **English**, **Hindi**, **Telugu**, and **one more language of your choice**. Ask your AI Agent to design a BPE tokenizer in such a way that:
10:
11:- you have **10 000 tokens** (your vocab) overall for all languages,
12:- $(\text{Total English tokens}) / (\text{Total English words})$ must be **1.2 or less** — call this $X_1$
13:- similarly ratios for Hindi, Telugu and another language are $X_2$, $X_3$, $X_4$
14:- sort $X_1, X_2, X_3, X_4$ — say $X_4$ is largest and $X_1$ is least
15:- your **assignment score** is $1000 / (X_4 - X_1)$
16:
17:### What you are submitting
18:
19:1. A **widget** that shows these ratios, token statistics and calculations, and your self score
20:2. Allows the grader to **see and download** your tokenizer (list of all tokens)
21:3. A **URL** for this widget on Netlify (or anywhere else you want to host)
22:4. **Please remember** that graders will run your tokenizer themselves to confirm your scores — be careful when you present claims about your numbers
23:
24:### How we mapped the brief
25:
26:| Brief | This folder |
27:|-------|-------------|

# Multilingual BPE tokenizer — India Wikipedia

This repository is the solution to the tokenizer assignment below (English, Hindi, Telugu, Sanskrit; shared 10 000-token vocab; score $1000 / (X_{\max}-X_{\min})$).

---

## Assignment

Your assignment would be to pick India's page on Wikipedia in **English**, **Hindi**, **Telugu**, and **one more language of your choice**. Ask your AI Agent to design a BPE tokenizer in such a way that:

- you have **10 000 tokens** (your vocab) overall for all languages,
- $(\text{Total English tokens}) / (\text{Total English words})$ must be **1.2 or less** — call this $X_1$
- similarly ratios for Hindi, Telugu and another language are $X_2$, $X_3$, $X_4$
- sort $X_1, X_2, X_3, X_4$ — say $X_4$ is largest and $X_1$ is least
- your **assignment score** is $1000 / (X_4 - X_1)$

### What you are submitting

1. A **widget** that shows these ratios, token statistics and calculations, and your self score
2. Allows the grader to **see and download** your tokenizer (list of all tokens)
3. A **URL** for this widget on Netlify (or anywhere else you want to host)
4. **Please remember** that graders will run your tokenizer themselves to confirm your scores — be careful when you present claims about your numbers

### How we mapped the brief

| Brief | This folder |
|-------|-------------|
| English, Hindi, Telugu | India Wikipedia pages (`en` / `hi` / `te`) |
| One more language | **Sanskrit** (`sa`) |
| “Words” in the ratio | Pretokenized word count $D_L$ (scripts: Latin, Devanagari, Telugu + digits) |
| $X_L$ | $T_L / D_L$ after encoding language $L$ |
| Shared vocab | **10 000** tokens for all four languages |

---

## Submission (Approach B)

| | |
|--|--|
| **Method** | Short BPE (~2 500 slots) + whole-word fill; languages still above $X=1.2$ get seats first (`deficit`) |
| **Self score** | **9237.39** |
| **Vocab size** | **10 000** |
| **$X_{\mathrm{EN}} \le 1.2$** | **yes** (1.158) |
| **Slideshow** | https://revant-tokenizer-slides.surge.sh (mirror: https://tokenizer-india-slides-rev.netlify.app) |
| **Widget** | https://tokenizer-india-b-opt-rev-28915.netlify.app |
| **Local packs** | [`demo/slides/`](demo/slides/) · [`demo/widget/`](demo/widget/) |
| **Tokenizer file** | [`approaches/b/vocab_optimized_fullpage.json`](approaches/b/vocab_optimized_fullpage.json) |
| **Trainer** | [`approaches/b/train_optimized_b.py`](approaches/b/train_optimized_b.py) |
| **Downloadable token list** | `demo/slides/tokens.txt` / `tokenizer.json` (same on widget) |

### Per-language metrics (Approach B · primary corpus)

| Language | Words $D$ | Tokens $T$ | $X = T/D$ | ≤ 1.2? |
|----------|------------:|-------------:|------------:|:------:|
| English | 30 789 | 35 649 | **1.158** | yes |
| Hindi | 13 630 | 14 788 | **1.085** | yes |
| Telugu | 4 053 | 4 254 | **1.050** | yes |
| Sanskrit | 2 091 | 2 322 | **1.110** | yes |

$$
X_{\max} = 1.15785,\quad X_{\min} = 1.04959,\quad
\text{gap} = 0.10826,\quad
\text{score} = 1000 / 0.10826 \approx \mathbf{9237.39}
$$

All four $X \le 1.2$. UNK count on these training pages: **0**.

### Vocab distribution (Approach B)

| Component | Count |
|-----------|------:|
| Stage-1 BPE (characters + merges) | **2 500** (≈ **2 297** merge rules) |
| Stage-2 whole words | **7 500** |
| Priority fill while some $X > 1.2$ | EN **2 713** · HI **1 345** · TE **1 278** · SA **867** |
| Leftover fill after all $X \le 1.2$ | **1 297** |
| **Total** | **10 000** |

Types: stored as full words vs subword fallback

| Language | Unique on page | Full-word in vocab | Not listed (BPE pieces) |

Method notes: [`approaches/b/README.md`](approaches/b/README.md).

---

## Training data

Primary pages: India (same topic) in four languages, under [`datasets/full_page_md/`](datasets/full_page_md/). Scoring applies a light clean (keep link labels, drop URLs).

| A | Pure BPE | 10k | ~1500 | 1.216 | 1.207 | 1.635 | 1.874 | no |

\*Hard ok ≈ $X_{\mathrm{EN}}\le 1.2$ and vocab ≤ 10 000.  
†E as stored on full pages exceeds the vocab cap.

D / champion maximize the formula with page-specific multi-word slabs; comparison only — **not** the claimed product tokenizer.

---

```

## Assignment

Build a **multilingual BPE tokenizer** trained on India's Wikipedia page in **4 languages**: English, Hindi, Telugu, + one language of choice.

**Requirements:**
1. Shared vocab of exactly **10,000 tokens** across all 4 languages combined
2. For each language, compute $X_L = \text{(tokens produced)} / \text{(word count)}$
3. Sort the four $X$ values — call the min $X_{\min}$, max $X_{\max}$
4. **Score** = $1000 / (X_{\max} - X_{\min})$ — i.e., you want the ratios as *tight/close together* as possible across languages, all while each staying reasonably efficient
5. English ratio $X_1$ must be **≤ 1.2** (roughly: don't waste more than 20% extra tokens vs. word count)

**Deliverables:**
1. A **widget** displaying the ratios, token stats, and self-computed score
2. Ability for graders to **view and download** the tokenizer (full token list)
3. A **hosted URL** (Netlify or similar)
4. Caution: graders **re-run your tokenizer themselves** — don't overstate results

## What this repo already has

This repo is a completed solution:
- **Languages**: English, Hindi, Telugu, Sanskrit
- **Approach B** (the submission): short BPE (~2,500 slots) + whole-word fill, prioritizing languages still above X=1.2
- **Self score: 9237.39**, vocab exactly 10,000, all four $X \le 1.2$ (0.05–0.16 range, tight spread)
- Widget hosted at netlify, slideshow at surge.sh, tokenizer file at `approaches/b/vocab_optimized_fullpage.json`
- Several alternative approaches (A–E, Champion) explored and compared in `approaches/`

# tsai-skills

**Grok skills** + headless fetch toolkit for **Axiom Learning OS**
(The School of AI).

**Host:** `https://axiom.theschoolofai.in`

Agent interface is the skill `axiom-learning-os` (not an MCP server). Day-to-day
data pull is cookie + CLI; discovery used Zen + Firefox DevTools once.

## Quick start — what am I enrolled in?

```bash
cd ~/timepass/tsai-skills

# 1) Enrolled courses + standing (cookie auto-resolved — see below)
./scripts/fetch.sh enrolled-summary
# same as: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m tsai_skills.fetch enrolled-summary
```

No env or manual cookie export is required for normal use — a hardcoded
session token is bundled (gitignored) and auto-refreshed when it expires.

## Cookie auth & auto-refresh

All Learning OS APIs authenticate with a single NextAuth cookie:

```
Cookie: __Secure-next-auth.session-token=<token>
```

No Bearer token, no API key, no CSRF for GETs. The CLI resolves the token
in priority order and **refreshes automatically** when the session is dead:

```
1. --token / AXIOM_SESSION_TOKEN / AXIOM_COOKIE_FILE   (explicit override)
2. .secrets/session_token                               (persisted cookie file)
3. src/tsai_skills/local_cookie.py                      (hardcoded fallback, gitignored)
        │
        ▼
   probe GET /api/auth/session
        │
        ├─ valid (has user) → proceed
        └─ empty {} / 401  → auto-refresh
                │
                ▼
           read Zen cookies.sqlite
           (~/.zen/f7zfdnyw.Default (release), or $ZEN_PROFILE)
                │
                ▼
           write .secrets/session_token + update local_cookie.py
                │
                ▼
           re-probe once → proceed or fail with “log into Axiom in Zen”
```

### What you need for auto-refresh

- **Zen Browser** (or Firefox) logged into `https://axiom.theschoolofai.in`.
- Default profile path: `~/.zen/f7zfdnyw.Default (release)` — override with
  `export ZEN_PROFILE=/path/to/profile`.
- The browser does **not** need to be running; `cookies.sqlite` is read from
  disk (copied to a temp dir if the profile is locked).

### Manual refresh

```bash
./scripts/export-cookie.sh          # pull from Zen → .secrets/session_token
```

### When auto-refresh fails

The session cookie in the browser is itself expired or missing. Fix:

1. Open Zen, go to `https://axiom.theschoolofai.in`, log in with Google.
2. Re-run `./scripts/fetch.sh session` (auto-refresh will pick up the new cookie).

Auto-refresh **only reads** the browser cookie store — it never automates
Google OAuth or stores passwords.

### Rotating the hardcoded cookie

`src/tsai_skills/local_cookie.py` is gitignored. After a successful refresh
(or manual export), the file is auto-updated. To set it by hand:

```bash
echo '"""Local hardcoded session cookie — gitignored, do not commit."""
SESSION_TOKEN = "eyJ…your-token…"' > src/tsai_skills/local_cookie.py
```

### Disabling auto-refresh

```bash
./scripts/fetch.sh courses --no-refresh          # fail instead of reading browser
./scripts/fetch.sh courses --skip-auth-probe     # skip probe entirely (fast, unsafe)
```

## Fetch any entity

```bash
./scripts/fetch.sh --list-entities

./scripts/fetch.sh courses
./scripts/fetch.sh sessions --course-id cmq97i5kn032208o8xu5dab4q
./scripts/fetch.sh grades-summary
./scripts/fetch.sh lessons --course-id cmq97i5kn032208o8xu5dab4q
./scripts/fetch.sh media --course-id cmq97i5kn032208o8xu5dab4q

./scripts/fetch.sh course-bundle \
  --course-id cmq97i5kn032208o8xu5dab4q \
  --out-dir out/course_cmq97i5kn032208o8xu5dab4q

./scripts/fetch.sh all --out-dir out/all
```

Default module entry is fetch:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m tsai_skills enrolled-summary
```

### Legacy narrow collector (sessions + assignments only)

```bash
./skill-dev/scripts/collect-course.sh cmq97i5kn032208o8xu5dab4q
```

## Skills

| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| [`skills/axiom-learning-os/`](skills/axiom-learning-os/) | Canonical skill (auth → scope → fetch) |
| [`.grok/skills/axiom-learning-os`](.grok/skills/) | Symlink so Grok auto-discovers the skill |
| `skills/…/references/api-endpoints.md` | Field-level API catalog |

Invoke with `/axiom-learning-os` or natural language (“what courses am I enrolled in?”).

## Docs (skill development)

Full map: [`skill-dev/`](skill-dev/).

| Doc | Purpose |
|-----|---------|
| [skill-dev/docs/AUTH.md](skill-dev/docs/AUTH.md) | Cookie auth for every API call |
| [skill-dev/docs/API_SURFACE.md](skill-dev/docs/API_SURFACE.md) | Verified endpoint map |
| [skill-dev/docs/COLLECTING.md](skill-dev/docs/COLLECTING.md) | Sessions + assignments collector notes |
| [skill-dev/docs/AGENT_PLAYBOOK.md](skill-dev/docs/AGENT_PLAYBOOK.md) | Expand extraction for new entities |
| [skill-dev/docs/REVERSE_ENGINEERING.md](skill-dev/docs/REVERSE_ENGINEERING.md) | How APIs were discovered |

## Mental model

1. Log in once with **Google** via **NextAuth** in the browser.
2. Reuse cookie `__Secure-next-auth.session-token` for same-origin `/api/*` GETs.
3. No Bearer token; CSRF not required for GETs.

```
Cookie: __Secure-next-auth.session-token
    ├─ /api/auth/session
    ├─ /api/courses
    ├─ /api/courses/{id}/sessions     (+ lesson markdown, video HTML)
    ├─ /api/assignments?courseId=
    ├─ /api/grades?view=summaries
    └─ /api/dashboard/student
```

## Layout

```
tsai-skills/
  skills/                    # source of truth for Grok skills
    axiom-learning-os/
  .grok/skills/              # symlinks → skills/* (Grok discovery)
  src/tsai_skills/           # Python package (fetch / collect / client)
  scripts/                   # export-cookie, fetch (runtime)
  skill-dev/                 # docs, fixtures, legacy collect-course
    docs/
    fixtures/                # anonymized JSON for tests
    scripts/collect-course.sh
  tests/
  out/                       # gitignored live dumps
  .secrets/                  # gitignored tokens
```

## Example course id

- **ERA V5:** `cmq97i5kn032208o8xu5dab4q`
- Always resolve live ids via `./scripts/fetch.sh courses` if enrollment changes.

## Safety

- Do not commit `.secrets/`, `local_cookie.py`, live cookies, or personal course dumps.
- On HTTP 401 / empty session, auto-refresh kicks in (see above); if that fails, re-login in Zen.
- Auto-refresh only reads the browser cookie store — no OAuth automation, no passwords stored.
- Own-account data only (same access as the UI).

## Install / tests

```bash
# optional editable install for console scripts tsai-fetch / tsai-collect
pip install -e .

PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

14:
15:Headless **fetch** of the signed-in student's Learning OS data.
16:Base: `https://axiom.theschoolofai.in`. Repo root = directory with `src/tsai_skills/`.
17:
18:**Leading idea:** treat the SPA's `/api/*` GETs as the only data plane — same cookie, same JSON the UI already uses.

21:
22:Cookie is resolved automatically (no manual env required for normal use):
23:
24:1. `--token` / `AXIOM_SESSION_TOKEN` / `AXIOM_COOKIE_FILE` if set  
25:2. `.secrets/session_token`  
26:3. **Hardcoded fallback** in `src/tsai_skills/local_cookie.py` (gitignored) + package default  
27:4. On dead session: **auto-refresh** from Zen profile cookies.sqlite  
28:   (`~/.zen/f7zfdnyw.Default (release)`, override with `ZEN_PROFILE`)
29:
30:`./scripts/fetch.sh` calls `ensure_authenticated_token()` → probes `/api/auth/session` →
31:if empty/`{}` or bad, pulls a fresh `__Secure-next-auth.session-token` from the browser
32:DB, writes `.secrets/session_token` + updates `local_cookie.py`, re-probes once.

42:cd <repo-root>
43:./scripts/fetch.sh session          # identity probe (refreshes cookie if needed)
44:./scripts/fetch.sh enrolled-summary # default first real call
45:```
46:
47:**Done when:** JSON includes a non-empty `user` (for `session`) or course data.
48:Exit 2 → log into https://axiom.theschoolofai.in in Zen, retry.
49:
50:### 2. Resolve scope
51:
52:Map the user question to the **narrowest** entity. Discover course ids from live data.
53:
54:```bash
55:./scripts/fetch.sh --list-entities
56:./scripts/fetch.sh enrolled-summary
57:```
58:
59:| Branch (user intent) | Entity | Needs |
60:|----------------------|--------|--------|
61:| What am I enrolled in / overview | `enrolled-summary` | — |
62:| Profile only | `me` | — |
63:| Classes / lectures / syllabus | `sessions` | `--course-id` |
64:| Lesson text | `lessons` | `--course-id` |
65:| YouTube / GMeet | `media` | `--course-id` |
66:| Assignments / due dates | `assignments` | `--course-id` |
67:| My upload / links | `submission` | `--assignment-id` |
68:| Scores / feedback | `grades` or `grades-summary` | optional `--course-id` |

70:| Rank / weak areas | `dashboard-student` | — |
71:| Quizzes | `quizzes` | `--course-id` |
72:| Flashcards | `flashcards` | `--course-id` |
73:| Announcements | `announcements` | `--course-id` |
74:| Bell feed | `notifications` | — |
75:| Full course dump | `course-bundle` | `--course-id --out-dir …` |
76:| Every enrolled course | `all` | `--out-dir …` |
77:

83:./scripts/fetch.sh <entity> [flags]
84:```

# Axiom Learning OS

Headless **fetch** of the signed-in student's Learning OS data.
Base: `https://axiom.theschoolofai.in`. Repo root = directory with `src/tsai_skills/`.

**Leading idea:** treat the SPA's `/api/*` GETs as the only data plane — same cookie, same JSON the UI already uses.

## Auth (built-in)

Cookie is resolved automatically (no manual env required for normal use):

1. `--token` / `AXIOM_SESSION_TOKEN` / `AXIOM_COOKIE_FILE` if set  
2. `.secrets/session_token`  
3. **Hardcoded fallback** in `src/tsai_skills/local_cookie.py` (gitignored) + package default  
4. On dead session: **auto-refresh** from Zen profile cookies.sqlite  
   (`~/.zen/f7zfdnyw.Default (release)`, override with `ZEN_PROFILE`)

`./scripts/fetch.sh` calls `ensure_authenticated_token()` → probes `/api/auth/session` →
if empty/`{}` or bad, pulls a fresh `__Secure-next-auth.session-token` from the browser
DB, writes `.secrets/session_token` + updates `local_cookie.py`, re-probes once.

**Done when refresh fails:** user must be logged into Axiom in Zen; then re-run.
Manual: `./scripts/export-cookie.sh`. Detail: `skill-dev/docs/AUTH.md`.

## Steps

### 1. Fetch (auth is automatic)

```bash
cd <repo-root>
./scripts/fetch.sh session          # identity probe (refreshes cookie if needed)
./scripts/fetch.sh enrolled-summary # default first real call
```

**Done when:** JSON includes a non-empty `user` (for `session`) or course data.
Exit 2 → log into https://axiom.theschoolofai.in in Zen, retry.

### 2. Resolve scope

Map the user question to the **narrowest** entity. Discover course ids from live data.

```bash
./scripts/fetch.sh --list-entities
./scripts/fetch.sh enrolled-summary
```

| Branch (user intent) | Entity | Needs |
|----------------------|--------|--------|
| What am I enrolled in / overview | `enrolled-summary` | — |
| Profile only | `me` | — |
| Classes / lectures / syllabus | `sessions` | `--course-id` |
| Lesson text | `lessons` | `--course-id` |
| YouTube / GMeet | `media` | `--course-id` |
| Assignments / due dates | `assignments` | `--course-id` |
| My upload / links | `submission` | `--assignment-id` |
| Scores / feedback | `grades` or `grades-summary` | optional `--course-id` |
| One assignment score | `assignment-grade` | `--assignment-id` |
| Rank / weak areas | `dashboard-student` | — |
| Quizzes | `quizzes` | `--course-id` |
| Flashcards | `flashcards` | `--course-id` |
| Announcements | `announcements` | `--course-id` |
| Bell feed | `notifications` | — |
| Full course dump | `course-bundle` | `--course-id --out-dir …` |
| Every enrolled course | `all` | `--out-dir …` |

**Done when:** One primary entity (and ids) is chosen. Prefer parse-over-fetch: lesson markdown and video embeds already sit on `sessions` (`lessons` / `media`).

### 3. Answer

```bash
./scripts/fetch.sh <entity> [flags]
```

**Done when:** CLI exit 0; reply uses **titles, dates, scores** (CUIDs only when needed);
no secrets written into git-tracked paths.

Field shapes: [references/api-endpoints.md](references/api-endpoints.md) · `skill-dev/docs/API_SURFACE.md`.

## Guardrails

- Own-account data only (UI-equivalent access).
- Cookie files stay under `.secrets/` / gitignored `local_cookie.py` — never commit tokens.
- Auto-refresh only **reads** the browser cookie store; it does not automate Google OAuth.
- `login.axiom.co` observability product is out of scope.

No TSAI references found in this repo — that's likely an external grading platform I don't have access to. You'd need to check the TSAI portal/dashboard directly.

## Python `collections.Counter` cheatsheet

```python
from collections import Counter

# Create
c = Counter(['a', 'b', 'a', 'c', 'b', 'a'])      # from iterable
c = Counter("aabbc")                              # from string
c = Counter({'a': 3, 'b': 2})                     # from dict
c = Counter(a=3, b=2, c=1)                        # from kwargs

# Access
c['a']          # 3  (count)
c['z']          # 0  (missing key -> 0, no KeyError)

# Update
c['a'] += 1
c.update(['a', 'd'])       # add counts
c.subtract(['a', 'b'])     # subtract counts (can go negative)

# Common queries
c.most_common()        # [('a', 3), ('b', 2), ...] sorted desc
c.most_common(2)        # top 2
sum(c.values())         # total count
list(c.elements())       # expand back to items (repeated by count)
+c                       # drop zero/negative counts (unary plus)

# Arithmetic (combines two Counters)
c1 + c2     # add counts (drops <=0 results)
c1 - c2     # subtract, keep only positive
c1 & c2     # min per key (intersection)
c1 | c2     # max per key (union)

# Convert
dict(c)          # plain dict
sorted(c)         # sorted keys
sorted(c.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])  # manual sort by count

# Reset
c.clear()
```

**Quick recipes**
```python
# Most frequent word count in text
Counter(text.split()).most_common(5)

# Check anagram
Counter(s1) == Counter(s2)

# Count char frequencies
Counter(s)
```
what are more helpful methods on counter object

Beyond the basics, here are the less obvious/more useful ones:

```python
from collections import Counter

c = Counter(a=3, b=1, c=0, d=-2)

# --- Membership / iteration ---
'a' in c              # True (key exists) — same as regular dict
len(c)                 # number of distinct keys (including 0/negative counts)
list(c)                # just the keys

# --- elements() ---
list(c.elements())     
# ['a','a','a','b']  -> zero/negative counts are SKIPPED automatically
# useful for "expand counts back into a multiset/list"

# --- unary +/- ---
+c   # Counter({'a': 3, 'b': 1})       -> keeps only counts > 0
-c   # Counter({'d': 2})                -> flips sign, keeps only counts > 0
     # (i.e. -c gives you the originally-negative entries, made positive)

# --- total() (Python 3.10+) ---
c.total()    # sum of all counts, same as sum(c.values()) but built-in

# --- most_common(n) with n=None ---
c.most_common()      # ALL items sorted by count desc (ties keep insertion order)
c.most_common(None)  # same as above, explicit

# --- update() vs subtract() nuance ---
c.update(a=1)         # ADDS to count (not overwrite!) -> common gotcha
c['a'] = 1            # this OVERWRITES (plain dict assignment)

# --- update/subtract accept Counter, dict, iterable, or kwargs ---
c.update(Counter(x=2))
c.update({'x': 2})
c.update(['x', 'x'])
c.update(x=2)

# --- Comparison operators (Python 3.10+) ---
Counter(a=1, b=2) <= Counter(a=2, b=2, c=1)   # True: subset (every count <=)
Counter(a=1) < Counter(a=1, b=1)               # proper subset

# --- copy ---
c2 = c.copy()   # shallow copy, avoids mutating original

# --- Getting the min/least common ---
c.most_common()[:-4:-1]   # bottom 3, reversed trick (careful with negatives)
min(c, key=c.get)          # key with smallest count
```

**Handy gotchas to remember**
- `Counter[missing_key]` → `0`, never raises `KeyError` (unlike plain dict).
- `c.update(x)` **adds**; `c[x] = n` **overwrites**. Easy to mix up.
- `+c` / arithmetic ops (`+`, `-`, `&`, `|`) silently **drop non-positive results**.
- `elements()` silently **skips** zero/negative counts — won't error, just omits them.

1:# tsai-skills
2:
3:**Grok skills** + headless fetch toolkit for **Axiom Learning OS**
4:(The School of AI).
5:
6:**Host:** `https://axiom.theschoolofai.in`
7:
8:Agent interface is the skill `axiom-learning-os` (not an MCP server). Day-to-day
9:data pull is cookie + CLI; discovery used Zen + Firefox DevTools once.
10:
11:## Quick start — what am I enrolled in?
12:
13:```bash
14:cd ~/timepass/tsai-skills
15:
16:# 1) Enrolled courses + standing (cookie auto-resolved — see below)
17:./scripts/fetch.sh enrolled-summary
18:# same as: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m tsai_skills.fetch enrolled-summary
19:```
20:
21:No env or manual cookie export is required for normal use — a hardcoded
22:session token is bundled (gitignored) and auto-refreshed when it expires.
23:
24:## Cookie auth & auto-refresh
25:
26:All Learning OS APIs authenticate with a single NextAuth cookie:
27:
28:```
29:Cookie: __Secure-next-auth.session-token=<token>
30:```
31:
32:No Bearer token, no API key, no CSRF for GETs. The CLI resolves the token
33:in priority order and **refreshes automatically** when the session is dead:
34:
35:```
36:1. --token / AXIOM_SESSION_TOKEN / AXIOM_COOKIE_FILE   (explicit override)
37:2. .secrets/session_token                               (persisted cookie file)
38:3. src/tsai_skills/local_cookie.py                      (hardcoded fallback, gitignored)
39:        │
40:        ▼
41:   probe GET /api/auth/session
42:        │
43:        ├─ valid (has user) → proceed
44:        └─ empty {} / 401  → auto-refresh
45:                │
46:                ▼
47:           read Zen cookies.sqlite
48:           (~/.zen/f7zfdnyw.Default (release), or $ZEN_PROFILE)
49:                │
50:                ▼
51:           write .secrets/session_token + update local_cookie.py
52:                │
53:                ▼
54:           re-probe once → proceed or fail with “log into Axiom in Zen”
55:```
56:
57:### What you need for auto-refresh
58:
59:- **Zen Browser** (or Firefox) logged into `https://axiom.theschoolofai.in`.
60:- Default profile path: `~/.zen/f7zfdnyw.Default (release)` — override with
61:  `export ZEN_PROFILE=/path/to/profile`.
62:- The browser does **not** need to be running; `cookies.sqlite` is read from
63:  disk (copied to a temp dir if the profile is locked).
64:
65:### Manual refresh
66:
67:```bash
68:./scripts/export-cookie.sh          # pull from Zen → .secrets/session_token
69:```
70:
71:### When auto-refresh fails
72:
73:The session cookie in the browser is itself expired or missing. Fix:
74:
75:1. Open Zen, go to `https://axiom.theschoolofai.in`, log in with Google.
76:2. Re-run `./scripts/fetch.sh session` (auto-refresh will pick up the new cookie).
77:
78:Auto-refresh **only reads** the browser cookie store — it never automates
79:Google OAuth or stores passwords.
80:
81:### Rotating the hardcoded cookie
82:
83:`src/tsai_skills/local_cookie.py` is gitignored. After a successful refresh
84:(or manual export), the file is auto-updated. To set it by hand:
85:
86:```bash
87:echo '"""Local hardcoded session cookie — gitignored, do not commit."""
88:SESSION_TOKEN = "eyJ…your-token…"' > src/tsai_skills/local_cookie.py
89:```
90:
91:### Disabling auto-refresh
92:
93:```bash
94:./scripts/fetch.sh courses --no-refresh          # fail instead of reading browser
95:./scripts/fetch.sh courses --skip-auth-probe     # skip probe entirely (fast, unsafe)
96:```

# tsai-skills

**Grok skills** + headless fetch toolkit for **Axiom Learning OS**
(The School of AI).

**Host:** `https://axiom.theschoolofai.in`

Agent interface is the skill `axiom-learning-os` (not an MCP server). Day-to-day
data pull is cookie + CLI; discovery used Zen + Firefox DevTools once.

## Quick start — what am I enrolled in?

```bash
cd ~/timepass/tsai-skills

# 1) Enrolled courses + standing (cookie auto-resolved — see below)
./scripts/fetch.sh enrolled-summary
# same as: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m tsai_skills.fetch enrolled-summary
```

No env or manual cookie export is required for normal use — a hardcoded
session token is bundled (gitignored) and auto-refreshed when it expires.

## Cookie auth & auto-refresh

All Learning OS APIs authenticate with a single NextAuth cookie:

```
Cookie: __Secure-next-auth.session-token=<token>
```

No Bearer token, no API key, no CSRF for GETs. The CLI resolves the token
in priority order and **refreshes automatically** when the session is dead:

```
1. --token / AXIOM_SESSION_TOKEN / AXIOM_COOKIE_FILE   (explicit override)
2. .secrets/session_token                               (persisted cookie file)
3. src/tsai_skills/local_cookie.py                      (hardcoded fallback, gitignored)
        │
        ▼
   probe GET /api/auth/session
        │
        ├─ valid (has user) → proceed
        └─ empty {} / 401  → auto-refresh
                │
                ▼
           read Zen cookies.sqlite
           (~/.zen/f7zfdnyw.Default (release), or $ZEN_PROFILE)
                │
                ▼
           write .secrets/session_token + update local_cookie.py
                │
                ▼
           re-probe once → proceed or fail with “log into Axiom in Zen”
```

### What you need for auto-refresh

- **Zen Browser** (or Firefox) logged into `https://axiom.theschoolofai.in`.
- Default profile path: `~/.zen/f7zfdnyw.Default (release)` — override with
  `export ZEN_PROFILE=/path/to/profile`.
- The browser does **not** need to be running; `cookies.sqlite` is read from
  disk (copied to a temp dir if the profile is locked).

### Manual refresh

```bash
./scripts/export-cookie.sh          # pull from Zen → .secrets/session_token
```

### When auto-refresh fails

The session cookie in the browser is itself expired or missing. Fix:

1. Open Zen, go to `https://axiom.theschoolofai.in`, log in with Google.
2. Re-run `./scripts/fetch.sh session` (auto-refresh will pick up the new cookie).

Auto-refresh **only reads** the browser cookie store — it never automates
Google OAuth or stores passwords.

### Rotating the hardcoded cookie

`src/tsai_skills/local_cookie.py` is gitignored. After a successful refresh
(or manual export), the file is auto-updated. To set it by hand:

```bash
echo '"""Local hardcoded session cookie — gitignored, do not commit."""
SESSION_TOKEN = "eyJ…your-token…"' > src/tsai_skills/local_cookie.py
```

### Disabling auto-refresh

```bash
./scripts/fetch.sh courses --no-refresh          # fail instead of reading browser
./scripts/fetch.sh courses --skip-auth-probe     # skip probe entirely (fast, unsafe)
```

## Fetch any entity

```bash
./scripts/fetch.sh --list-entities

./scripts/fetch.sh courses
./scripts/fetch.sh sessions --course-id cmq97i5kn032208o8xu5dab4q
./scripts/fetch.sh grades-summary
./scripts/fetch.sh lessons --course-id cmq97i5kn032208o8xu5dab4q
./scripts/fetch.sh media --course-id cmq97i5kn032208o8xu5dab4q

./scripts/fetch.sh course-bundle \
  --course-id cmq97i5kn032208o8xu5dab4q \
  --out-dir out/course_cmq97i5kn032208o8xu5dab4q

./scripts/fetch.sh all --out-dir out/all
```

Default module entry is fetch:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m tsai_skills enrolled-summary
```

### Legacy narrow collector (sessions + assignments only)

```bash
./skill-dev/scripts/collect-course.sh cmq97i5kn032208o8xu5dab4q
```

## Skills

| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| [`skills/axiom-learning-os/`](skills/axiom-learning-os/) | Canonical skill (auth → scope → fetch) |
| [`.grok/skills/axiom-learning-os`](.grok/skills/) | Symlink so Grok auto-discovers the skill |
| `skills/…/references/api-endpoints.md` | Field-level API catalog |

Invoke with `/axiom-learning-os` or natural language (“what courses am I enrolled in?”).

## Docs (skill development)

Full map: [`skill-dev/`](skill-dev/).

| Doc | Purpose |
|-----|---------|
| [skill-dev/docs/AUTH.md](skill-dev/docs/AUTH.md) | Cookie auth for every API call |
| [skill-dev/docs/API_SURFACE.md](skill-dev/docs/API_SURFACE.md) | Verified endpoint map |
| [skill-dev/docs/COLLECTING.md](skill-dev/docs/COLLECTING.md) | Sessions + assignments collector notes |
| [skill-dev/docs/AGENT_PLAYBOOK.md](skill-dev/docs/AGENT_PLAYBOOK.md) | Expand extraction for new entities |
| [skill-dev/docs/REVERSE_ENGINEERING.md](skill-dev/docs/REVERSE_ENGINEERING.md) | How APIs were discovered |

## Mental model

1. Log in once with **Google** via **NextAuth** in the browser.
2. Reuse cookie `__Secure-next-auth.session-token` for same-origin `/api/*` GETs.
3. No Bearer token; CSRF not required for GETs.

```
Cookie: __Secure-next-auth.session-token
    ├─ /api/auth/session
    ├─ /api/courses
    ├─ /api/courses/{id}/sessions     (+ lesson markdown, video HTML)
    ├─ /api/assignments?courseId=
    ├─ /api/grades?view=summaries
    └─ /api/dashboard/student
```

## Layout

```
tsai-skills/
  skills/                    # source of truth for Grok skills
    axiom-learning-os/
  .grok/skills/              # symlinks → skills/* (Grok discovery)
  src/tsai_skills/           # Python package (fetch / collect / client)
  scripts/                   # export-cookie, fetch (runtime)
  skill-dev/                 # docs, fixtures, legacy collect-course
    docs/
    fixtures/                # anonymized JSON for tests
    scripts/collect-course.sh
  tests/
  out/                       # gitignored live dumps
  .secrets/                  # gitignored tokens
```

## Example course id

- **ERA V5:** `cmq97i5kn032208o8xu5dab4q`
- Always resolve live ids via `./scripts/fetch.sh courses` if enrollment changes.

## Safety

- Do not commit `.secrets/`, `local_cookie.py`, live cookies, or personal course dumps.
- On HTTP 401 / empty session, auto-refresh kicks in (see above); if that fails, re-login in Zen.
- Auto-refresh only reads the browser cookie store — no OAuth automation, no passwords stored.
- Own-account data only (same access as the UI).

## Install / tests

```bash
# optional editable install for console scripts tsai-fetch / tsai-collect
pip install -e .

PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

---
name: axiom-learning-os
description: >
  Pull student data from TSAI Axiom Learning OS (axiom.theschoolofai.in) via
  cookie-auth JSON APIs. Use when the user asks about enrolled courses, ERA V5
  / course progress, sessions or lectures, assignments or submissions, grades
  or class standing, quizzes, flashcards, announcements, or to dump Learning
  OS data. Also when another skill needs live Axiom course state.
metadata:
  short-description: "Fetch TSAI Axiom Learning OS student data"
---

# Axiom Learning OS

Headless **fetch** of the signed-in student's Learning OS data.
Base: `https://axiom.theschoolofai.in`. Repo root = directory with `src/tsai_skills/`.

**Leading idea:** treat the SPA's `/api/*` GETs as the only data plane — same cookie, same JSON the UI already uses.

## Auth (built-in)

Cookie is resolved automatically (no manual env required for normal use):

1. `--token` / `AXIOM_SESSION_TOKEN` / `AXIOM_COOKIE_FILE` if set  
2. `.secrets/session_token`  
3. **Hardcoded fallback** in `src/tsai_skills/local_cookie.py` (gitignored) + package default  
4. On dead session: **auto-refresh** from Zen profile cookies.sqlite  
   (`~/.zen/f7zfdnyw.Default (release)`, override with `ZEN_PROFILE`)

`./scripts/fetch.sh` calls `ensure_authenticated_token()` → probes `/api/auth/session` →
if empty/`{}` or bad, pulls a fresh `__Secure-next-auth.session-token` from the browser
DB, writes `.secrets/session_token` + updates `local_cookie.py`, re-probes once.

**Done when refresh fails:** user must be logged into Axiom in Zen; then re-run.
Manual: `./scripts/export-cookie.sh`. Detail: `skill-dev/docs/AUTH.md`.

## Steps

### 1. Fetch (auth is automatic)

```bash
cd <repo-root>
./scripts/fetch.sh session          # identity probe (refreshes cookie if needed)
./scripts/fetch.sh enrolled-summary # default first real call
```

**Done when:** JSON includes a non-empty `user` (for `session`) or course data.
Exit 2 → log into https://axiom.theschoolofai.in in Zen, retry.

### 2. Resolve scope

Map the user question to the **narrowest** entity. Discover course ids from live data.

```bash
./scripts/fetch.sh --list-entities
./scripts/fetch.sh enrolled-summary
```

| Branch (user intent) | Entity | Needs |
|----------------------|--------|--------|
| What am I enrolled in / overview | `enrolled-summary` | — |
| Profile only | `me` | — |
| Classes / lectures / syllabus | `sessions` | `--course-id` |
| Lesson text | `lessons` | `--course-id` |
| YouTube / GMeet | `media` | `--course-id` |
| Assignments / due dates | `assignments` | `--course-id` |
| My upload / links | `submission` | `--assignment-id` |
| Scores / feedback | `grades` or `grades-summary` | optional `--course-id` |
| One assignment score | `assignment-grade` | `--assignment-id` |
| Rank / weak areas | `dashboard-student` | — |
| Quizzes | `quizzes` | `--course-id` |
| Flashcards | `flashcards` | `--course-id` |
| Announcements | `announcements` | `--course-id` |
| Bell feed | `notifications` | — |
| Full course dump | `course-bundle` | `--course-id --out-dir …` |
| Every enrolled course | `all` | `--out-dir …` |

**Done when:** One primary entity (and ids) is chosen. Prefer parse-over-fetch: lesson markdown and video embeds already sit on `sessions` (`lessons` / `media`).

### 3. Answer

```bash
./scripts/fetch.sh <entity> [flags]
```

**Done when:** CLI exit 0; reply uses **titles, dates, scores** (CUIDs only when needed);
no secrets written into git-tracked paths.

Field shapes: [references/api-endpoints.md](references/api-endpoints.md) · `skill-dev/docs/API_SURFACE.md`.

## Guardrails

- Own-account data only (UI-equivalent access).
- Cookie files stay under `.secrets/` / gitignored `local_cookie.py` — never commit tokens.
- Auto-refresh only **reads** the browser cookie store; it does not automate Google OAuth.
- `login.axiom.co` observability product is out of scope.

# Axiom Learning OS — verified API endpoints (2026-07)

Load this file when parsing fields, debugging a response, or adding a fetch entity.
Default skill path stays in `SKILL.md` steps — do not re-list this table there.

Base URL: `https://axiom.theschoolofai.in`  
Auth: `Cookie: __Secure-next-auth.session-token=<token>` only.

Live-probed against a student session. 404 paths are listed as non-endpoints.

CLI maps 1:1 via `python3 -m tsai_skills.fetch <entity>` (see `--list-entities`).

---

## Identity & enrollment

### `GET /api/auth/session`

| Auth | Status | Body |
|------|--------|------|
| Valid | 200 | `{ user: { name, email, image, id, role }, expires, loginAt }` |
| Missing | 200 | `{}` |

### `GET /api/me`

Student profile:

- `id`, `name`, `email`, `avatarUrl`, `role`
- `githubId`, `githubUsername` (may be null)
- `createdAt`, `lastLoginAt`

### `GET /api/courses`

**Enrolled courses** array. Each item:

- `id`, `title`, `description`, `accentColor`, `status` (`active`), `createdAt`, `chatEnabled`

### `GET /api/courses/{courseId}`

Same shape as a single course object from the list (detail view).

### `GET /api/dashboard`

Home shell:

- `courses[]` — includes `totalSessions`, `completedSessions` plus course fields
- `deadlines[]`
- `activity[]` — `{ id, type, title, description, timestamp }`

---

## Course content

### `GET /api/courses/{courseId}/sessions`

Primary **class/lecture** payload. Array of:

| Field | Extract |
|-------|---------|
| `id`, `title`, `order`, `status` | Session identity |
| `opensAt`, `closesAt` | Availability |
| `studioVideoHtml` | Lecture iframe HTML (parse YouTube) |
| `gmeetVideoHtml` | Live meet HTML |
| `lessons[]` | `title`, `markdownContent` (often full), `markdownUrl`, `estimatedMinutes` |
| `quizzes[]`, `assignments[]` | Nested stubs (prefer dedicated list endpoints) |

### `GET /api/assignments?courseId=`

| Field | Extract |
|-------|---------|
| `id`, `title`, `sessionId`, `courseId` | Identity |
| `descriptionMarkdown` | Full brief |
| `dueAt`, `maxPoints`, `status`, `kind` | Logistics |
| `parts[]` | `label`, `type` (e.g. `link`), `points`, `prompt` |
| `hasUserSubmission`, `submissionCount` | Progress |
| `rubricJson`, `assignmentRepoUrl` | Extra |

### `GET /api/assignments/{id}/submission`

Own submission or structured object with:

- `submittedAt`, `isLate`, `answers[]` with `answer.links[]`, `earnedPoints`
- `submittedBy: { userId, name, isMe }`

May be `null` if not submitted.

### `GET /api/assignments/{id}/grade`

- `score`, `extraPoints`, `feedback`, `gradedAt`, `isDraft`
- Nested `assignment`, `grader`
- `null` if not graded yet

### `GET /api/quizzes?courseId=`

List items:

- `id`, `title`, `sessionId`, `courseId`
- `timeLimit`, `opensAt`, `closesAt`, `maxAttempts`, `questionCount`, `order`
- `hasUserAttempt`, `attemptCount`, `_count`

### `GET /api/quizzes/{quizId}`

Metadata only (no full question bank in this response). Includes `course`, `session.status`.

### `GET /api/courses/{id}/flashcards`

Cards:

- `prompt`, `answer`, `type` (e.g. `mcq`), `contentJson` (options)
- `sessionId`, `sessionTitle`, `order`
- `myRating`, `attemptedCount`, `masteredCount`

### `GET /api/courses/{id}/announcements`

- `title`, `content`, `isPinned`, `createdAt`
- `author: { id, name, avatarUrl }`

### `GET /api/courses/{id}/chat/channels`

- `type`: `general` \| `session` \| `dm`
- `label`, `sessionTitle`, `unread`, `unreadMentions`, `canPost`, `hasMessages`

Message history is separate (`…/chat/channels/{id}/messages`) — optional expansion.

---

## Grades & progress

### `GET /api/grades`

Optional `?courseId=`. Array of grade rows:

- `score`, `extraPoints`, `feedback`, `gradedAt`
- `assignmentId` / `quizId`, nested `assignment` or `quiz`

### `GET /api/grades?view=summaries`

Used by SPA `/grades` page:

- `courseId`, `courseTitle`, `totalEarned`, `totalPossible`
- `gradedItemCount`, `overallPercentage`

### `GET /api/dashboard/student`

| Key | Contents |
|-----|----------|
| `classStanding` | `percentile`, `rank`, `totalStudents`, `averageScore`, `classAverage`, `status` |
| `overallHealth` | quiz/assignment completion, `avgQuizScore`, `pendingItems`, `weakAreaCount` |
| `scoreTrajectory[]` | assignment/quiz scores over time |
| `weakAreas[]` | quizzes with wrong question snippets |
| `actionItems[]` | todo-like items |
| `feed[]` | browse/feed cards (papers, links) |

### `GET /api/dashboard/flashcards`

Per-course: `total`, `attempted`, `unattempted`, `mastered`.

---

## Chrome / misc

| Path | Notes |
|------|-------|
| `GET /api/notifications?limit=N` | `{ items: [{ type, title, body, linkUrl, meta, readAt, createdAt }] }` |
| `GET /api/me/chat/courses` | Chat rail: `unread`, `handsUp` |
| `GET /api/daily-check` | `{ items: [] }` |
| `GET /api/invites/pending` | Array (often empty) |
| `POST /api/activity/heartbeat` | Presence; ignore for extraction |
| `POST /api/auth/_log` | NextAuth client log; ignore |

---

## Not found (do not use)

Probed 404:

- `/api/announcements?courseId=` (use course-scoped path)
- `/api/me/profile`
- `/api/leaderboard`, `/api/courses/{id}/leaderboard`
- `/api/courses/{id}/members`
- `/api/browse`, `/api/feed`, `/api/courses/{id}/feed`

---

## Parsing without new HTTP

```text
sessions.json
  → lessons[].markdownContent     full lesson text
  → studioVideoHtml               YouTube embed src
  → gmeetVideoHtml / markdown     meet.google.com links
```

CLI helpers:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m tsai_skills.fetch lessons --course-id CID
PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m tsai_skills.fetch media --course-id CID
```

35:            raw = token

43:        req = urllib.request.Request(
44:            url,
45:            method=method,

47:                "Accept": "application/json",
48:                "Cookie": self._cookie_header(),
49:                "User-Agent": DEFAULT_UA,

53:            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=self.timeout_sec) as resp:

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AxiomClient:
    session_token: str
    base_url: str = DEFAULT_BASE
    timeout_sec: float = 60.0

    def _cookie_header(self) -> str:
        token = self.session_token.strip()
        if not token:
            raise AuthError("empty session cookie/token")
        if "session-token=" in token or token.lower().startswith("cookie:"):
            raw = token
            if raw.lower().startswith("cookie:"):
                raw = raw.split(":", 1)[1].strip()
            return raw
        return f"__Secure-next-auth.session-token={token}"

    def _request(self, method: str, path: str) -> tuple[int, Any]:
        url = self.base_url.rstrip("/") + path
        req = urllib.request.Request(
            url,
            method=method,
            headers={
                "Accept": "application/json",
                "Cookie": self._cookie_header(),
                "User-Agent": DEFAULT_UA,
            },
        )
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=self.timeout_sec) as resp:
                body = resp.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
                status = resp.getcode() or 200
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            body = e.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
            status = e.code
        except urllib.error.URLError as e:
            raise ApiError(f"network error for {path}: {e}") from e

        if not body.strip():
            data: Any = None
        else:
            try:
                data = json.loads(body)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                data = body

        if status == 401:
            raise AuthError(
                f"Unauthorized (HTTP 401) for {path}: cookie/session invalid or missing"
            )
        if status >= 400:
            raise ApiError(f"HTTP {status} for {path}: {str(body)[:300]}")
        return status, data

    def get_session(self) -> Any:
        """GET /api/auth/session — identity probe ({} when unauthenticated)."""
        _, data = self._request("GET", "/api/auth/session")
        return data

import json, urllib.request, urllib.parse

TOKEN = open('.secrets/session_token').read().strip()

CID_COURSE = 'cmq97i5kn032208o8xu5dab4q'
CID_CHAN = 'cmqhkz740003c09p1j88ahyg5'

def fetch(before=None):
    path = f'/api/courses/{CID_COURSE}/chat/channels/{CID_CHAN}/messages'
    if before:
        path += '?' + urllib.parse.urlencode({'before': before})
    req = urllib.request.Request(BASE+path, headers={'Cookie': f'__Secure-next-auth.session-token={TOKEN}', 'Accept':'application/json'})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as r:
        return json.loads(r.read().decode())

all_msgs = {}
before = None
pages = 0
while True:
    page = fetch(before)
    pages += 1
    if not page:
        break
    for m in page:
        all_msgs[m['id']] = m
    oldest = min(page, key=lambda m: m['createdAt'])
    if before == oldest['createdAt']:
        break
    before = oldest['createdAt']
    if pages > 20:
        break
print('pages', pages, 'total unique', len(all_msgs))
times = sorted(m['createdAt'] for m in all_msgs.values())
print('range', times[0], times[-1])

"""HTTP client for Axiom Learning OS (cookie auth only)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

DEFAULT_BASE = "https://axiom.theschoolofai.in"
DEFAULT_UA = "tsai-skills/0.1 (+headless; https://axiom.theschoolofai.in)"


class AuthError(RuntimeError):
    """Missing, invalid, or rejected session cookie."""


class ApiError(RuntimeError):
    """Non-auth HTTP/API failure."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AxiomClient:
    session_token: str
    base_url: str = DEFAULT_BASE
    timeout_sec: float = 60.0

    def _cookie_header(self) -> str:
        token = self.session_token.strip()
        if not token:
            raise AuthError("empty session cookie/token")
        if "session-token=" in token or token.lower().startswith("cookie:"):
            raw = token
            if raw.lower().startswith("cookie:"):
                raw = raw.split(":", 1)[1].strip()
            return raw
        return f"__Secure-next-auth.session-token={token}"

    def _request(self, method: str, path: str) -> tuple[int, Any]:
        url = self.base_url.rstrip("/") + path
        req = urllib.request.Request(
            url,
            method=method,
            headers={
                "Accept": "application/json",
                "Cookie": self._cookie_header(),
                "User-Agent": DEFAULT_UA,
            },
        )
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=self.timeout_sec) as resp:
                body = resp.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
                status = resp.getcode() or 200
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            body = e.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
            status = e.code
        except urllib.error.URLError as e:
            raise ApiError(f"network error for {path}: {e}") from e

        if not body.strip():
            data: Any = None
        else:
            try:
                data = json.loads(body)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                data = body

        if status == 401:
            raise AuthError(
                f"Unauthorized (HTTP 401) for {path}: cookie/session invalid or missing"
            )
        if status >= 400:
            raise ApiError(f"HTTP {status} for {path}: {str(body)[:300]}")
        return status, data

    def get_session(self) -> Any:
        """GET /api/auth/session — identity probe ({} when unauthenticated)."""
        _, data = self._request("GET", "/api/auth/session")
        return data

---
name: axiom-learning-os
description: >
  Pull student data from TSAI Axiom Learning OS (axiom.theschoolofai.in) via
  cookie-auth JSON APIs. Use when the user asks about enrolled courses, ERA V5
  / course progress, sessions or lectures, assignments or submissions, grades
  or class standing, quizzes, flashcards, announcements, or to dump Learning
  OS data. Also when another skill needs live Axiom course state.
metadata:
  short-description: "Fetch TSAI Axiom Learning OS student data"
---

# Axiom Learning OS

Headless **fetch** of the signed-in student's Learning OS data.
Base: `https://axiom.theschoolofai.in`. Repo root = directory with `src/tsai_skills/`.

**Leading idea:** treat the SPA's `/api/*` GETs as the only data plane — same cookie, same JSON the UI already uses.

## Auth (built-in)

Cookie is resolved automatically (no manual env required for normal use):

1. `--token` / `AXIOM_SESSION_TOKEN` / `AXIOM_COOKIE_FILE` if set  
2. `.secrets/session_token`  
3. **Hardcoded fallback** in `src/tsai_skills/local_cookie.py` (gitignored) + package default  
4. On dead session: **auto-refresh** from Zen profile cookies.sqlite  
   (`~/.zen/f7zfdnyw.Default (release)`, override with `ZEN_PROFILE`)

`./scripts/fetch.sh` calls `ensure_authenticated_token()` → probes `/api/auth/session` →
if empty/`{}` or bad, pulls a fresh `__Secure-next-auth.session-token` from the browser
DB, writes `.secrets/session_token` + updates `local_cookie.py`, re-probes once.

**Done when refresh fails:** user must be logged into Axiom in Zen; then re-run.
Manual: `./scripts/export-cookie.sh`. Detail: `skill-dev/docs/AUTH.md`.

## Steps

### 1. Fetch (auth is automatic)

```bash
cd <repo-root>
./scripts/fetch.sh session          # identity probe (refreshes cookie if needed)
./scripts/fetch.sh enrolled-summary # default first real call
```

**Done when:** JSON includes a non-empty `user` (for `session`) or course data.
Exit 2 → log into https://axiom.theschoolofai.in in Zen, retry.

### 2. Resolve scope

Map the user question to the **narrowest** entity. Discover course ids from live data.

```bash
./scripts/fetch.sh --list-entities
./scripts/fetch.sh enrolled-summary
```

| Branch (user intent) | Entity | Needs |
|----------------------|--------|--------|
| What am I enrolled in / overview | `enrolled-summary` | — |
| Profile only | `me` | — |
| Classes / lectures / syllabus | `sessions` | `--course-id` |
| Lesson text | `lessons` | `--course-id` |
| YouTube / GMeet | `media` | `--course-id` |
| Assignments / due dates | `assignments` | `--course-id` |
| My upload / links | `submission` | `--assignment-id` |
| Scores / feedback | `grades` or `grades-summary` | optional `--course-id` |
| One assignment score | `assignment-grade` | `--assignment-id` |
| Rank / weak areas | `dashboard-student` | — |
| Quizzes | `quizzes` | `--course-id` |
| Flashcards | `flashcards` | `--course-id` |
| Announcements | `announcements` | `--course-id` |
| Bell feed | `notifications` | — |
| Full course dump | `course-bundle` | `--course-id --out-dir …` |
| Every enrolled course | `all` | `--out-dir …` |

**Done when:** One primary entity (and ids) is chosen. Prefer parse-over-fetch: lesson markdown and video embeds already sit on `sessions` (`lessons` / `media`).

### 3. Answer

```bash
./scripts/fetch.sh <entity> [flags]
```

**Done when:** CLI exit 0; reply uses **titles, dates, scores** (CUIDs only when needed);
no secrets written into git-tracked paths.

Field shapes: [references/api-endpoints.md](references/api-endpoints.md) · `skill-dev/docs/API_SURFACE.md`.

## Guardrails

- Own-account data only (UI-equivalent access).
- Cookie files stay under `.secrets/` / gitignored `local_cookie.py` — never commit tokens.
- Auto-refresh only **reads** the browser cookie store; it does not automate Google OAuth.
- `login.axiom.co` observability product is out of scope.

# Axiom Learning OS — verified API endpoints (2026-07)

Load this file when parsing fields, debugging a response, or adding a fetch entity.
Default skill path stays in `SKILL.md` steps — do not re-list this table there.

Base URL: `https://axiom.theschoolofai.in`  
Auth: `Cookie: __Secure-next-auth.session-token=<token>` only.

Live-probed against a student session. 404 paths are listed as non-endpoints.

CLI maps 1:1 via `python3 -m tsai_skills.fetch <entity>` (see `--list-entities`).

---

## Identity & enrollment

### `GET /api/auth/session`

| Auth | Status | Body |
|------|--------|------|
| Valid | 200 | `{ user: { name, email, image, id, role }, expires, loginAt }` |
| Missing | 200 | `{}` |

### `GET /api/me`

Student profile:

- `id`, `name`, `email`, `avatarUrl`, `role`
- `githubId`, `githubUsername` (may be null)
- `createdAt`, `lastLoginAt`

### `GET /api/courses`

**Enrolled courses** array. Each item:

- `id`, `title`, `description`, `accentColor`, `status` (`active`), `createdAt`, `chatEnabled`

### `GET /api/courses/{courseId}`

Same shape as a single course object from the list (detail view).

### `GET /api/dashboard`

Home shell:

- `courses[]` — includes `totalSessions`, `completedSessions` plus course fields
- `deadlines[]`
- `activity[]` — `{ id, type, title, description, timestamp }`

---

## Course content

### `GET /api/courses/{courseId}/sessions`

Primary **class/lecture** payload. Array of:

| Field | Extract |
|-------|---------|
| `id`, `title`, `order`, `status` | Session identity |
| `opensAt`, `closesAt` | Availability |
| `studioVideoHtml` | Lecture iframe HTML (parse YouTube) |
| `gmeetVideoHtml` | Live meet HTML |
| `lessons[]` | `title`, `markdownContent` (often full), `markdownUrl`, `estimatedMinutes` |
| `quizzes[]`, `assignments[]` | Nested stubs (prefer dedicated list endpoints) |

### `GET /api/assignments?courseId=`

| Field | Extract |
|-------|---------|
| `id`, `title`, `sessionId`, `courseId` | Identity |
| `descriptionMarkdown` | Full brief |
| `dueAt`, `maxPoints`, `status`, `kind` | Logistics |
| `parts[]` | `label`, `type` (e.g. `link`), `points`, `prompt` |
| `hasUserSubmission`, `submissionCount` | Progress |
| `rubricJson`, `assignmentRepoUrl` | Extra |

### `GET /api/assignments/{id}/submission`

Own submission or structured object with:

- `submittedAt`, `isLate`, `answers[]` with `answer.links[]`, `earnedPoints`
- `submittedBy: { userId, name, isMe }`

May be `null` if not submitted.

### `GET /api/assignments/{id}/grade`

- `score`, `extraPoints`, `feedback`, `gradedAt`, `isDraft`
- Nested `assignment`, `grader`
- `null` if not graded yet

### `GET /api/quizzes?courseId=`

List items:

- `id`, `title`, `sessionId`, `courseId`
- `timeLimit`, `opensAt`, `closesAt`, `maxAttempts`, `questionCount`, `order`
- `hasUserAttempt`, `attemptCount`, `_count`

### `GET /api/quizzes/{quizId}`

Metadata only (no full question bank in this response). Includes `course`, `session.status`.

### `GET /api/courses/{id}/flashcards`

Cards:

- `prompt`, `answer`, `type` (e.g. `mcq`), `contentJson` (options)
- `sessionId`, `sessionTitle`, `order`
- `myRating`, `attemptedCount`, `masteredCount`

### `GET /api/courses/{id}/announcements`

## Byte Pair Encoding (BPE)

BPE is a subword tokenization algorithm, originally a data compression technique (Gage, 1994), adapted for NLP (Sennrich et al., 2016) and used in GPT, RoBERTa, etc.

### Core idea
Start with characters (or bytes), and iteratively merge the most frequent adjacent pair into a new token — building up a vocabulary of subwords from the bottom up.

### Training algorithm

1. **Initialize vocabulary** with all individual characters/bytes present in the training corpus. Represent each word as a sequence of these symbols, usually with an end-of-word marker (e.g. `low</w>` → `l o w </w>`).

2. **Count all adjacent symbol pairs** across the corpus (weighted by word frequency).

3. **Find the most frequent pair** — e.g. `("l", "o")` appears 500 times.

4. **Merge that pair** into a new symbol (`"lo"`), add it to the vocabulary, and replace all occurrences of that pair in the corpus.

5. **Repeat** steps 2–4 for a fixed number of merges (or until vocab reaches a target size).

### Example

```
Corpus: low low low lower lower newest newest widest

Step 0: l o w </w>, l o w e r </w>, n e w e s t </w>, w i d e s t </w>
Step 1: merge (e, s) -> "es"   (most frequent pair)
Step 2: merge (es, t) -> "est"
Step 3: merge (est, </w>) -> "est</w>"
Step 4: merge (l, o) -> "lo"
... continues until merge budget exhausted
```

Final vocab = original chars + all learned merges (e.g. `lo`, `est</w>`, `low`, `newest`, ...).

### Encoding (applying BPE to new text)
Apply the **same merge rules in the order they were learned**, greedily, to any new word — splitting unknown words into known subwords/characters as a fallback. This is why BPE never produces an "unknown token" (unlike whole-word vocabularies) — anything decomposes to characters/bytes in the worst case.

### Key properties
- **Vocabulary size** is a tunable hyperparameter (number of merges + base alphabet).
- **Frequent words** end up as single tokens; **rare/unseen words** get split into smaller, still-meaningful subword pieces.
- Balances vocabulary size vs. sequence length — the trade-off the merge count controls.
- **Byte-level BPE** (GPT-2 style) starts from raw bytes (256 symbols) instead of Unicode characters, so it can represent *any* text without an unknown/OOV token at all.

# Axiom Learning OS

Headless **fetch** of the signed-in student's Learning OS data.
Base: `https://axiom.theschoolofai.in`. Repo root = directory with `src/tsai_skills/`.

**Leading idea:** treat the SPA's `/api/*` GETs as the only data plane — same cookie, same JSON the UI already uses.

## Auth (built-in)

Cookie is resolved automatically (no manual env required for normal use):

1. `--token` / `AXIOM_SESSION_TOKEN` / `AXIOM_COOKIE_FILE` if set  
2. `.secrets/session_token`  
3. **Hardcoded fallback** in `src/tsai_skills/local_cookie.py` (gitignored) + package default  
4. On dead session: **auto-refresh** from Zen profile cookies.sqlite  
   (`~/.zen/f7zfdnyw.Default (release)`, override with `ZEN_PROFILE`)

`./scripts/fetch.sh` calls `ensure_authenticated_token()` → probes `/api/auth/session` →
if empty/`{}` or bad, pulls a fresh `__Secure-next-auth.session-token` from the browser
DB, writes `.secrets/session_token` + updates `local_cookie.py`, re-probes once.

**Done when refresh fails:** user must be logged into Axiom in Zen; then re-run.
Manual: `./scripts/export-cookie.sh`. Detail: `skill-dev/docs/AUTH.md`.

## Steps

### 1. Fetch (auth is automatic)

```bash
cd <repo-root>
./scripts/fetch.sh session          # identity probe (refreshes cookie if needed)
./scripts/fetch.sh enrolled-summary # default first real call
```

**Done when:** JSON includes a non-empty `user` (for `session`) or course data.
Exit 2 → log into https://axiom.theschoolofai.in in Zen, retry.

### 2. Resolve scope

Map the user question to the **narrowest** entity. Discover course ids from live data.

```bash
./scripts/fetch.sh --list-entities
./scripts/fetch.sh enrolled-summary
```

| Branch (user intent) | Entity | Needs |
|----------------------|--------|--------|
| What am I enrolled in / overview | `enrolled-summary` | — |
| Profile only | `me` | — |
| Classes / lectures / syllabus | `sessions` | `--course-id` |
| Lesson text | `lessons` | `--course-id` |
| YouTube / GMeet | `media` | `--course-id` |
| Assignments / due dates | `assignments` | `--course-id` |
| My upload / links | `submission` | `--assignment-id` |
| Scores / feedback | `grades` or `grades-summary` | optional `--course-id` |
| One assignment score | `assignment-grade` | `--assignment-id` |
| Rank / weak areas | `dashboard-student` | — |
| Quizzes | `quizzes` | `--course-id` |
| Flashcards | `flashcards` | `--course-id` |
| Announcements | `announcements` | `--course-id` |
| Chat channels / unread | `chat-channels` | `--course-id` |
| Chat messages (latest page) | `chat-messages` | `--course-id --channel-id` |
| Chat messages (full history) | `chat-messages --all` | `--course-id --channel-id` |
| Bell feed | `notifications` | — |
| Full course dump | `course-bundle` | `--course-id --out-dir …` |
| Every enrolled course | `all` | `--out-dir …` |

**Done when:** One primary entity (and ids) is chosen. Prefer parse-over-fetch: lesson markdown and video embeds already sit on `sessions` (`lessons` / `media`).

### 3. Answer

```bash
./scripts/fetch.sh <entity> [flags]
```

**Done when:** CLI exit 0; reply uses **titles, dates, scores** (CUIDs only when needed);
no secrets written into git-tracked paths.

Field shapes: [references/api-endpoints.md](references/api-endpoints.md) · `skill-dev/docs/API_SURFACE.md`.

## Guardrails

- Own-account data only (UI-equivalent access).
- Cookie files stay under `.secrets/` / gitignored `local_cookie.py` — never commit tokens.
- Auto-refresh only **reads** the browser cookie store; it does not automate Google OAuth.
- `login.axiom.co` observability product is out of scope.

2. `.secrets/session_token`  
3. **Hardcoded fallback** in `src/tsai_skills/local_cookie.py` (gitignored) + package default  
4. On dead session: **auto-refresh** from Zen profile cookies.sqlite  
   (`~/.zen/f7zfdnyw.Default (release)`, override with `ZEN_PROFILE`)

`./scripts/fetch.sh` calls `ensure_authenticated_token()` → probes `/api/auth/session` →
if empty/`{}` or bad, pulls a fresh `__Secure-next-auth.session-token` from the browser
DB, writes `.secrets/session_token` + updates `local_cookie.py`, re-probes once.

**Done when refresh fails:** user must be logged into Axiom in Zen; then re-run.
Manual: `./scripts/export-cookie.sh`. Detail: `skill-dev/docs/AUTH.md`.

## Steps

### 1. Fetch (auth is automatic)

```bash
cd <repo-root>
./scripts/fetch.sh session          # identity probe (refreshes cookie if needed)
./scripts/fetch.sh enrolled-summary # default first real call
```

**Done when:** JSON includes a non-empty `user` (for `session`) or course data.
Exit 2 → log into https://axiom.theschoolofai.in in Zen, retry.

### 2. Resolve scope

Map the user question to the **narrowest** entity. Discover course ids from live data.

```bash
./scripts/fetch.sh --list-entities
./scripts/fetch.sh enrolled-summary
```

| Branch (user intent) | Entity | Needs |
|----------------------|--------|--------|
| What am I enrolled in / overview | `enrolled-summary` | — |
| Profile only | `me` | — |
| Classes / lectures / syllabus | `sessions` | `--course-id` |
| Lesson text | `lessons` | `--course-id` |
| YouTube / GMeet | `media` | `--course-id` |
| Assignments / due dates | `assignments` | `--course-id` |
| My upload / links | `submission` | `--assignment-id` |
| Scores / feedback | `grades` or `grades-summary` | optional `--course-id` |
| One assignment score | `assignment-grade` | `--assignment-id` |
| Rank / weak areas | `dashboard-student` | — |
| Quizzes | `quizzes` | `--course-id` |
| Flashcards | `flashcards` | `--course-id` |
| Announcements | `announcements` | `--course-id` |
| Chat channels / unread | `chat-channels` | `--course-id` |
| Chat messages (latest page) | `chat-messages` | `--course-id --channel-id` |
| Chat messages (full history) | `chat-messages --all` | `--course-id --channel-id` |
| Bell feed | `notifications` | — |
| Full course dump | `course-bundle` | `--course-id --out-dir …` |
| Every enrolled course | `all` | `--out-dir …` |

**Done when:** One primary entity (and ids) is chosen. Prefer parse-over-fetch: lesson markdown and video embeds already sit on `sessions` (`lessons` / `media`).

### 3. Answer

```bash
./scripts/fetch.sh <entity> [flags]
```

**Done when:** CLI exit 0; reply uses **titles, dates, scores** (CUIDs only when needed);
no secrets written into git-tracked paths.

Field shapes: [references/api-endpoints.md](references/api-endpoints.md) · `skill-dev/docs/API_SURFACE.md`.

## Guardrails

- Own-account data only (UI-equivalent access).
- Cookie files stay under `.secrets/` / gitignored `local_cookie.py` — never commit tokens.
- Auto-refresh only **reads** the browser cookie store; it does not automate Google OAuth.
- `login.axiom.co` observability product is out of scope.

14: 15:# 2. The dilemma before the algorithm 16: 17:Before we reach for any algorithm, it is worth feeling the problem that the algorithm exists to solve. Take a single sentence and try to split it in the two most obvious ways. The first way is to split it into individual characters, which gives you a tiny set of symbols to learn, since a couple of hundred characters cover most of English. The cost of that choice is that sequences become enormous, and the model spends a large part of its capacity rediscovering, over and over again, that the three characters t, h, and e tend to travel together as the word "the." The second way is to split the sentence into whole words, which gives you short sequences that are pleasant to work with. That middle path exists, it is called subword tokenization, and **Byte-Pair Encoding** is one well-known way to find it. Everything that follows is built on top of this felt problem, so it is worth spending real time here until the trade-off feels obvious rather than abstract. 25: 26: 27: 28: 29:> Goal: you should leave feeling, rather than just being told, that neither extreme is workable and that something in between is needed. 30: 31: 32:

Why tokenization is load-bearing 41: 42:Now that the trade-off is in your hands, it is worth making the stakes explicit, because tokenization is unusual among the decisions in a training pipeline. It is decided exactly once, before training begins, and everything downstream inherits it permanently. The length of every sequence, and therefore the compute spent on every sentence, is fixed by it. The set of things the model is even capable of spelling is fixed by it, because a string that never became a token has no symbol the model can ever produce. The fairness of the model across different languages is fixed by it. And the size of the embedding table, which is one of the largest single pieces of the whole model, is fixed by it. You cannot repair a bad tokenizer by training for longer, in the same … 43: 44:The clearest way to feel the cost is through the bill. Suppose your tokenizer splits Telugu into roughly three times as many tokens as it uses for the same meaning in English. Every Telugu user then pays close to three times the inference cost for the same request, and the model sees only about a third as much Telugu context inside the same fixed window. This is not a rounding error and it does not heal with scale, because a larger context window lifts both languages together and leaves the ratio between them untouched. This is the natural place for the Indic-script motivation to enter the session, not as a footnote at the end but as a direct consequence of a single early decision. 45: 46: 47: 48: 49:> A view of the tokenizer as a frozen decision, with a set of presets that lean the tokenizer toward characters, toward English words, or toward a balanced subword scheme, and a panel that traces how each downstream property changes as a result. 50: 51:
